senses.gloss: (b. h.; v. סַד) [to join, fasten; denom. יְסוֹד, whence יָסַד] to found, establish. Tanḥ.
units: <cite ref="Genesis 1:1">B’resh. 1</cite> <he>ובה … וי׳ ארץ</he> and with it (the Torah) he stretched the heavens and established the earth.
<cite ref="Megillah 3a">Meg. 3ᵃ</cite>; <cite ref="Shabbat 104a">Sabb. 104ᵃ</cite>; <cite ref="Sukkah 44a:10">Succ. 44ᵃ</cite> <he>וחזרו וִיסָדוּם</he> and they reintroduced them.

senses.gloss: to establish; to join in between. Y. Erub. V, 22ᶜ שער היסוד ששם היו מְיַיסְּדִין וכ׳ the Eastern Gate was named the Foundation Gate, because there they (in their meetings) established the decisions of the Law; a. e.—Part. pass. מְיוּסָּד.
units: <cite ref="Yoma 2a">Ib.</cite> <he>שער התווך שהוא מי׳ בין וכ׳</he> it was named the Middle Gate because it was fastened in between two gates; a. e.

<cite ref="Tosefta Bava Metzia 11:4">Tosef. B. Mets. XI, 4</cite> <he>לא יאמר לו הריני מייסד עמך מכנגד וכ׳</he> (not <he>עמו</he>) he has no right to say, I will help thee rebuild the party wall from where my (higher situated) ground commences and upward, <he>אלא מייסד עמו וכ׳</he> but he must help him build from the bottom (of the neighbor’s ground) &c.; Y. ib. X, beg. 12ᶜ; (<cite ref="Bava Batra 6b:12">B. Bath. 6ᵇ</cite> <he>מסייע מלמטה</he>). [<cite ref="Shir HaShirim Rabbah 1:2:6">Cant. R. to I, 2</cite> <he>שהרי חבירו בא ליַסֵּד עליו כן</he> the next following sentence comes to found upon it a base (thus proving that the reading is <he>דּוֹדֶיךָ</he> and not <he>דּוֹדַיִךְ</he>). Some eds. read <cite ref="L00565"><he>לימד</he></cite>; <cite ref="Mishnah Avodah Zarah 2:5">Ab. Zar. II, 5</cite> <he>חבירו מלמד</he>; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Nach 981:8">Yalk. Cant. 981</cite> <cite ref="M00473"><he>מוכיח</he></cite>.]

senses.gloss: to be established. Tanḥ. l. c. העולם לא נ׳ וכ׳ the world has been founded on nothing but the Law.
